correctness.rationale: The inspected verifier independently generates all simple games through five players both as antichains of minimal winning coalitions and as monotone Boolean tables and obtains identical universes. It checks properness, computes Shapley-Shubik both from pivotal-coalition weights and all permutations, computes Deegan-Packel exactly, requires a strict pairwise reversal for every disagreement, canonicalizes every five-player disagreement under all 120 relabelings, and reconstructs all nine classes from explicit weighted representations. It obtains the standard simple-game counts \(1,4,18,166,7579\), proper counts \(1,3,11,80,2645\), zero proper disagreements through four and exactly 460 at five, plus 16 unrestricted four-player disagreements all improper. An independent monotone-table replay reproduced the proper and divergence counts.

originality.rationale: Aziz's full primary paper defines and computationally compares classical power indices including Deegan-Packel and Shapley-Shubik, while Freixas–Marciniak establish a structural property satisfied by Shapley-Shubik but not Deegan-Packel. These sources show meaningful differences between the indices but do not identify the first proper simple-game size at which their weak rankings reverse. Targeted web and Resultary searches for the count 460, the nine classes, and the displayed weighted witness found no covering theorem or table.

value.rationale: Deegan-Packel and Shapley-Shubik are classical power indices with different interpretations, and properness is a standard structural restriction. The smallest proper electorate size at which the two indices strictly reverse a pairwise ranking is therefore a natural exact boundary; classifying all nine first obstruction types and showing they are weighted makes the result directly reusable for voting-power examples and benchmark tests.
residual_risks: An unindexed historical enumeration, thesis, classroom note or voting-game software table may contain the same five-player classification.

final_claim: Every proper simple game on at most four players has the same Deegan-Packel and Shapley-Shubik weak player ordering, while among the 2645 labelled proper five-player games exactly 460 have a strict ranking reversal; these form exactly nine isomorphism classes, all weighted, with the stated representatives, and unrestricted divergence already occurs for 16 improper four-player games.
scientific_limitations: An unindexed historical enumeration, thesis, classroom note or voting-game software table may contain the same five-player classification.
The result classifies weak-order disagreement only through five players and gives no larger-player frequency law.
